facts.text: Koppel was named after Arthur Koppel of the German firm Orenstein & Koppel, who owned 558 acres nearby by 1907.
In 1912, Koppel officially became a borough, and the next year Orenstein & Koppel donated land for its first school and town hall.
During World War I, the Office of Alien Property Custodian seized most of Orenstein & Koppel’s holdings in Koppel, selling much to the Koppel Industrial and Equipment Company.
The Pressed Steel Car Company operated in Koppel from 1919 to 1937, while Babcock & Wilcox ran plants there during the 1950s.
On June 20, 1907, newspapers heralded Koppel’s opening day, calling it a “new industrial town growing at a wonderful rate” on the Pittsburgh & Lake Erie Railroad.
Koppel’s old bridge over the Beaver River was replaced in a modern dedication, marking a key moment in the borough’s transportation history.
